author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
With China flexing its naval power across the Pacific and bilateral tensions running high, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is weighing a move long viewed as taboo – nuclear-powered submarines for the Maritime Self-Defence Force fleet.
“We will seriously consider [the possibility] in a concrete and realistic manner,” Takaichi told the Japanese parliament on October 14.
Yet with Tokyo set to revise its core security documents by year’s end, the proposal is dividing the ruling coalition.
The...
title: Eye on China: Japan reopens taboo debate over nuclear-powered submarines

author: Laura Zhou
description:
The debate over ethnic identity in Xinjiang has triggered an online clash between Chinese and Turkish social media users.
The row began earlier this month when a Turkish social media user recalled an encounter with a Uygur from Xinjiang, the region in China that is home to nearly 12 million mainly Muslim Turkic speakers.
The user wrote that the woman did not look Chinese, but when asked whether she considered herself Turkic, the woman responded: “No, I’m Chinese.” The user also called on her to...
title: War of words over Xinjiang erupts between Chinese and Turkish social media users

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China’s Liaoning aircraft carrier strike group sailed beyond the first island chain last week to reach the southernmost waters of the Philippines, suggesting an intent to position itself closer to ongoing US-Japan joint exercises.
Philippine news channel BNC reported that the carrier group reached about 25 nautical miles (46km) east-southeast of Balut Island, the southernmost point of the Philippines, before sailing northeast on Friday.
That positioned the warships past the first island chain, a...
title: China’s Liaoning carrier and USS Theodore Roosevelt may be in Philippine Sea at same time

author: Alcott Wei,William Zheng
description:
China’s five-year leadership cycle is getting under way at a provincial level, with new teams being installed in a process that offers important clues to the future of the Communist Party at a national level.
Last week, four provinces – Anhui, Henan, Shanxi and Xinjiang – wrapped up their respective party congresses and appointed new standing committees for the next five years.
The meetings were held a week before a key party gathering in Beijing – known as the fifth plenum – that runs from...
title: How China’s regional leadership changes offer clues to the future of the Communist Party

author: William Zheng
description:
Beijing pledged to support pro-unification forces in Taiwan on Sunday as it mounted a concerted publicity campaign on Sunday to mark the 81st anniversary of the end of Japanese colonial rule over the island.
October 25 was formally established by Beijing last year as an official memorial date known as “Taiwan Restoration Day”.
Speaking at an event in Fuzhou, the capital of Fujian province, on Sunday, Song Tao, the head of Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office, said the memorial day highlighted...
title: Beijing pledges to back Taiwan’s pro-unification ‘patriots’ as it marks key anniversary

author: Jevans Nyabiage
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping outlined Beijing’s formula for tackling African conflicts and hot-button issues during a meeting this month with visiting Togolese leader Faure Gnassingbe, framing it around four principles linking peace to development.
The principles focus on African-led security free from outside intervention; upholding sovereignty and UN Charter principles; rejecting force and sanctions and favouring ceasefires through dialogue; and focusing on both immediate security concerns and...
title: Will China’s 4 peace principles for tackling African conflicts work?

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Young Chinese people enjoy Japanese pop culture such as anime and music, but many draw a firm line at symbols of Japanese militarism.
That line was tested recently at Moscow State University, where Chinese students confronted a classmate wearing Japan’s rising sun flag in class and called for his repatriation, state-run newspaper Global Times reported on Sunday.
Many countries, including China, view the flag as a symbol of Japanese militarism and aggression. Japan’s Self-Defence Forces still use...
title: Fandom vs flag: why young Chinese embrace Japanese pop culture but reject war-era symbols
